times, oppose **Venus**. Where **Saturn** is influential, employ **Jupiter**. And take care that you remain in a certain perpetual motion according to your strength—provided you avoid exhaustion—so that you may oppose your own movement to external movements that might secretly harm you, and so that you may imitate celestial activity as much as you are able. If you can traverse wider spaces in your movements, you will better imitate the heavens and, being spread out across different areas, you will reach more of the celestial powers.

## How the members of our body are nourished by the comparison of the Moon to the signs and to the fixed stars.
### Chapter VII.

**Y**ou will be able to nourish the whole body in the manner we have described, but the head most especially, if you observe the **Planets** in **Aries**, or each in its first <term>domicile</term> <note>original: "domicilio"; the zodiac sign where a planet's influence is strongest</note>. For the region of the heart, look to **Leo**. For the stomach and liver, look to **Cancer** and **Sagittarius**, or at least in **Virgo**. You should also receive those things that specifically seek out that member. It is also useful to know which members each **Planet** governs in any given sign. You can also consult specifically for each person’s difference in age through the four ages of the **Moon**. For the **Moon** is "youthful" from the New Moon until the first <term>quadrature</term> <note>original: "quadraturam"; the first quarter phase, a 90-degree angle from the Sun</note>. From then until the Full Moon, she is youthful and in her prime. From there to the next quadrature, she is simultaneously in her prime and aging. From then until the <term>conjunction</term> <note>original: "coniunctionem"; the New Moon, when the Moon and Sun meet</note>, she is aged. Therefore, you will successfully apply the age of the **Moon** to the age of the body being treated, if at that time you receive her in aspect to any of the <term>Three Graces</term> <note>Ficino identifies the "Three Graces" as the Sun, Jupiter, and Venus, the most beneficial celestial bodies</note>. Indeed, such an aspect of the **Moon** always and quickly bestows grace-filled gifts. 

However, these gifts are not easily lasting or very great unless, beyond the gaze of the **Moon**, the **Graces** themselves also look upon one another—either already in aspect or about to be—either all three or at least two of them. Above all, the <term>fixed signs</term> <note>Leo, Aquarius, Taurus, and Scorpio; signs known for stability and endurance</note> provide lasting effects. These are **Leo**, **Aquarius**, **Taurus**, and **Scorpio**. If by chance you cannot conveniently direct the **Moon** to the gracious **Planets** at the present time, choose **fixed stars** possessing the nature of the **Graces**—that is, the nature of **Jupiter**, **Venus**, or the **Sun**—and choose the **Moon** directed toward them. Yet it is safer, meanwhile, for the **Moon** to approach **Jupiter** or **Venus**. For if the fixed stars act alone, they far exceed the human proportion—that is, the scale of a single man. They hold a more moderate proportion, however, with cities.

## On the virtues and use of the fixed stars.
### Chapter XIII.

**A**strologers hand down the tradition that certain greater stars discovered by **Mercury** possess the greatest authority. Such is the star in the twenty-second degree of **Aries**, **Andromeda’s Navel** <note>original: "umbilicus Andromedae"; the star Mirach</note>, which is of the nature of **Mercury** and **Venus**. Likewise, in the eighteenth degree of **Taurus** is the **Head of Algol** <note>original: "caput Algol"; traditionally considered a very malevolent star, but Ficino notes its uses</note>, possessing the nature of **Saturn** and **Jupiter**. They wish for the diamond and wormwood <note>original: "artemisiam"</note> to be subject to it, and they say it provides boldness and victory. In the twenty-second degree of the same sign are the **Pleiades**, a **Lunar** and **Martian** constellation. To this they subject crystal, the herb <term>diacedon</term> <note>likely a reference to a specific prepared herb or a variant of chicory</note>, and fennel seed. They believe these contribute to sharpening the sight. However, as for what some say about their usefulness for summoning demons, I judge that to be a fiction. **Aldebaran** <note>original: "Aldeboran"</note> is in the first or third degree of **Gemini**, of the nature of **Mars** and **Venus**. The **Goat** <note>original: "Hircus"; the star Capella</note> is in the thirteenth degree of the same sign, of the nature of **Jupiter** and **Saturn**. To this they subject the sapphire, <term>prase</term> <note>a leek-green variety of quartz</note>, mint, wormwood, and mandrake. They trust it helps toward attaining dignity and the favor of princes, unless perhaps this opinion deceives them. To that star they wish the agate stone, the herb woodruff <note>original: "matrisyluam"</note> to be subject, and they say it increases riches and glory. 

In the sixth or seventh degree of **Cancer** is the **Greater Dog** <note>original: "Canis maior"; the star Sirius</note>, of the nature of **Venus**; it presides over beryl, savin, wormwood, and dragonwort. It bestows favor. Likewise, in the seventeenth degree of the same is the **Lesser Dog** <note>original: "Canis minor"; the star Procyon</note>, of the nature of **Mercury** and **Mars**. To this they wish the agate stone, the <term>heliotrope</term> <note>original: "folsequium"; a flower that follows the sun</note>, and pennyroyal to be subject, and it bestows favor. In the twenty-first degree of **Leo** is the **Lion’s Heart** <note>original: "Cor Leonis"; the star Regulus</note>, a royal star of the nature of **Jupiter** and **Mars**. To this they believe the garnet stone, celandine, and mastic are subject; it represses melancholy and makes one temperate and gracious. In the nineteenth degree of **Virgo** is the **Tail of the Greater Bear** <note>original: "Cauda Ursae maioris"; the star Alkaid</note>, of the nature of **Venus** and the **Moon**. They believe its stone is the magnet and its herb is chicory, and it protects against robbers and poisonings. In the seventh degree of **Libra** is the **Right Wing of the Crow**. Likewise, in the twelfth and perhaps thirteenth of the same is the **Left Wing**, being both **Saturnian** and **Martian**. Its herbs are dock and henbane; they say that when used with a frog's tongue, it increases audacity. It can be harmful. In the fifteenth or sixteenth of the same is **Spica** <note>original: "spica"; the Ear of Grain in the constellation Virgo</note>, of the nature of **Venus** and **Mercury**. Following this are the emerald, sage, trefoil, <term>prorulla</term> <note>likely a botanical name for a small creeping plant or pearlwort</note>,

In the 16th degree of **Aquarius** is the **Tail of Capricorn** <note>the star Deneb Algedi</note>, of the nature of **Saturn** and **Mercury**. Following this are **Chalcedony**, **marjoram**, **catnip**, **mugwort**, and **mandrake**. They believe it provides favor in legal cases, increases wealth, and keeps a man and his home safe. In the 3rd degree of **Pisces** is the **Shoulder of the Horse** <note>the star Markab in Pegasus</note>, of **Jupiter** and **Mars**. <term>Thebit</term> <note>Thabit ibn Qurra, a 9th-century astronomer and mathematician</note> the philosopher teaches that to capture the virtue of any of these aforementioned stars, one should take its stone and its herb and make a gold or silver ring, in which you insert the stone with the herb placed underneath it, and wear it so it touches the skin. You should do this when the **Moon** joins that star, or looks upon it with a <term>trine</term> or <term>sextile</term> aspect <note>astrological angles of 120 and 60 degrees, considered harmonious</note>, and while the star is traveling through the mid-heaven or the ascendant. I, however, regarding things pertaining to such stars, would compose them into the form of a medicine rather than a ring, to be applied internally or externally, provided the opportunity of the aforementioned time is observed. Even so, the ancients greatly prized rings. For <term>Damis</term> and <term>Philostratus</term> <note>biographers of the philosopher Apollonius of Tyana</note> relate that <term>Hiarchas</term>, the prince of the Indian sages, crafted seven rings by a similar method, named after the seven stars <note>the seven classical planets</note>, and gave them to <term>Apollonius of Tyana</term>. He then wore each one on its respective day, distinguishing them according to the names of the days. Indeed, Hiarchas told Apollonius that his own grandfather, a philosopher, had lived one hundred and thirty years, perhaps relying on such a celestial gift. Apollonius himself later used them and, even in his hundredth year, they say he maintained the appearance of a young man. Finally, if such rings have any power from on high, I do not think it pertains so much to the soul or to the dense body, but rather to the <term>spirit</term> <note>original: "spiritum"; in Ficino's philosophy, a subtle vapor that links the physical body to the immaterial soul</note>. As the ring is gradually warmed, the spirit is affected in this or that way, so that it becomes firmer, clearer, more vigorous, milder, more serious, or more joyful. These affections then pass entirely into the body and, in a certain way, into the sensory soul, which often indulges the body. As for the promise that rings will be effective against demons or enemies, or for gaining favor from princes—this is either a fiction, or it stems from the fact that they make the spirit focused and firm, or even gentle, lovable in its obedience, and gracious. Now truly, if I were to say that celestial things—besides physical health—can contribute to talent, art, and fortune, I would not disagree with our <term>Thomas Aquinas</term>, who proves in the third book of the *Against the Gentiles* that something is imprinted on our body by the celestial bodies, by whose gift we are often disposed to choose what is better, even if we do not know the reason or the end. In such matters, he calls people "well-fortuned" and (agreeing with <term>Aristotle</term>) "well-born." He adds also that by celestial virtue, some become effective in certain outcomes of the arts (to use his words), just as a soldier is successful in conquering, a farmer in planting, and a doctor in healing. For just as herbs and stones have certain marvelous celestial powers beyond the nature of the elements, so too do some men in the arts. For me, however, it will be enough if celestial things, in whatever way through medicines—whether internal or external—contribute to prosperous health, provided that while we seek the health of the body, we lose nothing of the health of the soul. We should attempt nothing at all prohibited by holy religion. Moreover, in the completion of any work, let us hope for and seek the fruit of that work

<page-num>542</page-num>
<header>MARSILIO FICINO ON OBTAINING CELESTIAL LIFE</header>

# MARSILIO FICINO ON OBTAINING CELESTIAL LIFE

->*Concerning the dignities of the Planets in the signs to be observed for the use of medicines. Chapter IX.*<-

**S**aturn's houses are Aquarius and Capricorn. Its <term>exaltation</term> <note>a sign where a planet’s influence is particularly harmonious or heightened</note> is Libra. Jupiter's houses are Sagittarius and Pisces; its exaltation or kingdom is Cancer. Mars's domicile is Scorpio and Aries; its exaltation is Capricorn. The Sun's seat is indeed Leo; its kingdom is Aries. Venus's habitation is Taurus and Libra; its exaltation is Pisces. Mercury's houses are Virgo and Gemini; its kingdom is Virgo. The Moon's house is Cancer; her exaltation is Taurus. Saturn and Jupiter have <term>triplicity</term> <note>a group of three signs belonging to the same element</note> in the fiery and airy signs. The Sun in the fiery signs only. Mercury in the airy signs alone. Mars, Venus, and the Moon in the watery and earthy signs. 

Any planet besides the Sun and Moon possesses certain "ends" of its own in any sign, which we also call <term>terms</term> <note>original: "terminos"; specific degree ranges within a zodiac sign where a planet exerts extra influence</note>. Therefore, in Aries, Jupiter obtains the first six terms there. Venus the six following, Mercury the later eight, Mars five thereafter, and Saturn the last five. In Taurus, in a similar following order, Venus has eight ends, Mercury six, Jupiter eight, Saturn five, and finally Mars three. In Gemini, Mercury has six, Jupiter six, Venus five, Mars seven, and Saturn six. In Cancer, Mars seven, Venus six, Mercury as many, Jupiter seven, and Saturn four. In Leo, Jupiter six, Venus five, Saturn seven, Mercury six, and Mars as many. In Virgo, Mercury seven, Venus ten, Jupiter four, Mars seven, and Saturn two. In Libra, Saturn six, Mercury eight, Jupiter seven, Venus as many, and Mars two. In Scorpio, Mars seven, Venus four, Mercury eight, Jupiter five, and Saturn six. In Sagittarius, Jupiter twelve, Venus five, Mercury four, Saturn five, and Mars four. In Capricorn, Mercury seven, Jupiter seven, Venus eight, Saturn four, and Mars as many. In Aquarius, Mercury seven, Venus six, Jupiter seven, Mars five, and Saturn as many. In Pisces, Venus twelve, Jupiter four, Mercury three, Mars nine, and finally Saturn two. 

The Sun and Moon, however, have their ends by another rule. For the Sun indeed has six signs for its ends: Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, and Capricorn. But the Moon has the rest: Aquarius, Pisces, Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer. They believe, therefore, that the Sun and Moon have that same leadership and effect in these signs which the rest of the Planets are thought to have in their own terms. Besides terms, the Planets have their <term>faces</term> <note>original: "facies"</note> in the signs, which the Greeks call <term>Decans</term>, occupying ten degrees of a sign. In Aries, the first face is of Mars. The second is of the Sun, who follows Mars in the sky according to the <term>Chaldean order</term> <note>an ancient sequence of planets based on their perceived orbital speed: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon</note>. The third is of Venus, who succeeds the Sun in the sky. In Taurus, the first face is of Mercury, following Venus. The second is of the Moon, who succeeds Mercury. The third is of Saturn. For one must return to him, the number of Planets now being completed. In Gemini, the first face is of Jupiter, clearly following Saturn; the second of Mars; the third of the Sun in the same order, and similarly thereafter.

---

->*How we ought to use the Planets in Medicines. Chapter X.*<-

**W**e have recounted what dignities the Planets have in the signs so that whenever we are about to act or compose anything pertaining to some Planet, we may know to place it in its own dignities. This is especially important when it has leadership in our <term>revolution</term> <note>a yearly solar return chart</note> or <term>nativity</term> <note>original: "genesis"; the birth chart</note>. In such cases, even Saturn and Mars—who are otherwise to be suppressed—must nevertheless be strengthened by us if they happen to be the <term>significators</term> <note>planets that represent the person or their health in a chart</note> of our birth. 

Most truly, however, we will have made it worth the effort of this recount if, whenever we are about to use the benefit of the Moon, Venus, and Jupiter in preparing medicines, we take care lest they exist in the terms of Saturn or Mars. This is unless we are perhaps compelled either to restrain a dissolution and repress a fever through Saturn, or to warm very cold things and arouse sluggish ones through Mars; otherwise, we shall choose the terms of Jupiter and Venus. We shall also accept the terms of Mercury, especially to benefit "Mercurial" men. Nor should it escape us that men who are highly Mercurial—such as those who excel in talent, craftsmanship, and eloquence—are not insignificantly Solar as well. For Mercury is always full of Apollo <note>the Sun</note>. 

However, so that anyone may understand how we describe the figures in the sky: the sign that rises from the East into the borders <note>the horizon</note> we call the first house, the house of life. That which follows into the rising, the second; then the third, and others similarly. Thus in the seventh house is the sign which, now descending in the West, is positioned opposite the ascending sign.

Here the eighth house follows. The ninth house, however, <term>falls</term> <note>original: "cadit"; a "cadent" house is considered weak because it moves away from the vital "angles" or corners of the chart</note> from the <term>mid-heaven</term> <note>the highest point of the southern sky, also called the tenth house</note>, which forms the tenth house. The eleventh follows this. But the twelfth falls away from the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the eastern horizon or first house</note>. Therefore, so that the Planets may be powerful, they must be held in the **angles**, either of the East, the West, or on either side of the mid-heaven. They are most powerful in the angle of the ascendant, or in the tenth house which holds the mid-heaven above the head, or at least in the regions that immediately follow the angles. Nevertheless, they believe the Sun "rejoices" in the ninth house (which falls from the mid-heaven), and the Moon rejoices in the third, which is also a cadent house.

Among these matters, Astrologers want two rules to be kept in mind: one concerning the patient, the other concerning the physician. Namely, where the seventh house of the sick person is made unfortunate by **Saturn** and **Mars**, or if the lord of that house is unhappy, separate the physician from the sick person, if you believe Ptolemy. Furthermore, when choosing a physician, they command you to avoid those of a "Saturnine" or "Martial" nature; instead, seek one whose birth chart shows the sixth house to be fortunate, whether by the <term>aspect</term> <note>the geometric angle between planets</note> of the Sun, or through **Venus** or **Jupiter**, in whatever manner it may be. 

We call a sign or a Planet "unfortunate" because of **Saturn** or **Mars**—unless those signs are their own homes or kingdoms—when they are either located there or look upon that place in **opposition** or **quadrature** <note>a "square" aspect of 90 degrees, considered tense or difficult</note>. We call an aspect "opposite" between those things which differ by the longest possible interval. We call it "quadrate" (square) where one is distant from the other by a fourth part of the sky, that is, a space of three signs. However, **Saturn** and **Mars** harm other Planets less through conjunction when they look upon them as guests in their own home, kingdom, or <term>term</term> <note>see previous page; a specific degree range within a sign</note>. In the same way, the happy Planets are more beneficial when they receive others through a **sextile** <note>60 degrees</note> or **trine** <note>120 degrees</note> aspect, and even by conjunction, as we have said. Planets fear a conjunction with the Sun, but they rejoice in his aspect, namely the trine or sextile.

Furthermore, it is necessary to remember that **Aries** presides over the head and face; **Taurus** over the neck; **Gemini** over the arms and shoulders; **Cancer** over the chest, lungs, stomach, and upper arms; **Leo** over the heart, stomach, liver, back, and rear ribs; **Virgo** over the intestines and the bottom of the stomach; **Libra** over the kidneys, hip, and buttocks; **Scorpio** over the genitals, vulva, and womb; **Sagittarius** over the thigh and the area below the groin; **Capricorn** over the knees; **Aquarius** over the shins and calves; and **Pisces** over the feet. 

Being mindful of this order, you will beware of touching a limb with iron <note>performing surgery</note>, or fire, or <term>cupping glasses</term> <note>suction jars used to draw out blood or humors</note> when the **Moon** is traveling through its corresponding sign. For at that time, the Moon increases the <term>humors</term> <note>bodily fluids like blood, phlegm, and bile</note> in that limb, and their overflowing both prevents healing and burdens the power of the limb. You should observe, however, that at such a time it is opportune and successful to nourish the limb with certain friendly remedies applied either externally or internally. 

It is also useful to know which sign was ascending at your birth. For besides **Aries**, this sign also signifies the head for you, and in this sign, the **Moon** regards your head. Furthermore, when the **Moon** enters **Aries**, you may opportunely try baths and washings. When she is in **Cancer**, you may successfully receive medicine for thinning the blood, especially in the form of an <term>electuary</term> <note>a medicinal paste made with honey or syrup</note>. When she is in **Leo**, do not induce vomiting. When in **Libra**, she is suited for enemas. In **Scorpio**, do not even attempt baths; there are some who neither forbid nor command giving purgative medicine then. In **Capricorn**, it is harmful to take medicine; similarly in **Aquarius**. In **Pisces**, however, it is beneficial. 

As for which limbs each of the Planets occupies in any given sign, although it is necessary to know, it would be tedious to relate. Nor should Ptolemy’s precept regarding the purification of the bowels escape us: we approve of taking purgative medicine when the **Moon** is in **Cancer**, **Pisces**, or **Scorpio**, especially if the lord of the sign ascending at that time applies itself to a Planet running beneath the earth. But if the lord of the ascendant is joined meanwhile above the head with a Planet holding the mid-heaven, nausea and vomiting will be incited immediately. 

Finally, let us conclude with Galen, who argued that Astrology is necessary for the physician. Discussing <term>critical days</term> <note>days in the course of a disease when a major change or 'crisis' occurs</note>, he says: the opinion of the Egyptians is certain—that is, that the **Moon** signifies the daily condition of both the sick and the healthy, to such an extent that if the rays of **Jupiter** and **Venus** are mixed with the **Moon**, both will be well affected. But if those of **Saturn** or **Mars** are mixed, the opposite will be the case. But having wandered widely enough now, let us at last 

->return to spirit, life, and the **Graces**.<-

<meta>This page continues Marsilio Ficino's discourse on the "spirit"—a subtle, vaporous substance that Renaissance doctors believed linked the physical body to the immaterial soul. While the previous pages discussed the placement of planets in the zodiac, this section moves into the specific planetary "flavors" of this spirit and how to nourish it through diet and lifestyle.</meta>

<page-num>546</page-num>
<header>ON OBTAINING CELESTIAL LIFE. BOOK III</header>

...is transferred, propagates offspring, expands itself toward the pleasure of any sense, and flees from pain. In short, insofar as the **spirit** <note>The "spiritus" was a thin, airy substance in the body that acted as the "engine" for all biological and mental functions</note> leads the body toward life, movement, and propagation, it is considered **Jovial** <note>of Jupiter</note>, **Venereal** <note>of Venus</note>, and **Solar**. Insofar as it serves the mind for sensation and imagination, it is judged **Solar** and **Mercurial**; indeed, it is Mercurial everywhere, since it is so mobile, so easily changeable, and so adaptable. 

A healthy spirit generally does not possess much of **Saturn**, **Mars**, or the **Moon**; otherwise, from the first it would often be stupid, from the second furious, and from the last somewhat dull. For this reason, **Lunar** things—being thicker and simultaneously wetter—are quite foreign to the subtle and volatile nature of the spirit. Those things that are heavily **Saturnine** or excessively **Martial** are like poisons, naturally hostile to the spirit: the former because of extreme cold and dryness, the latter because of dryness and a devouring heat. 

Therefore, the nature of the spirit is judged to be primarily **Jovial** and **Solar**, then **Mercurial**, and in some way **Venereal**. By a more precise distinction: 
* The <term>natural spirit</term> <note>responsible for basic biological growth and nutrition</note> is properly dedicated to **Jupiter**.
* The <term>vital spirit</term> <note>responsible for life-force and heat, centered in the heart</note> is dedicated to the **Sun**.
* The <term>animal spirit</term> <note>from 'anima' (soul); responsible for thought, sensation, and movement</note> is dedicated to **Mercury**.

Therefore, when a situation requires you to help one of these three spirits, you will not easily be able to assist it if its "patron" planet is <term>unfortunate</term> <note>poorly placed in the sky</note> or weak. It is most difficult to help the **animal spirit** when **Mercury** is unhappily affected; for Mercury has such great authority over the animal spirit that he is said to both lull minds to sleep and rouse them with his <term>caduceus</term> <note>the staff of Mercury; here used as a metaphor for planetary influence</note>. This means that by his specific <term>aspect</term> <note>geometric relationship to other planets</note>, he is able to wonderfully dull or sharpen the intellect, and to weaken, strengthen, disturb, or calm it. 

Whenever you study how to cultivate a particular spirit, you must not only observe that its patron planet is fortunate and powerful, but you should also choose a **Moon** that is opportunely directed toward it. The substance of the spirit is never properly created or restored by the influence of **Saturn** alone; however, the spirit is always called back by him from external things to the innermost, and often from the lowest to the highest. Hence, Saturn leads one to contemplate more secret and higher things. Nevertheless, even if rarely, the power of **Mars** and **Saturn** can benefit the spirit as a medicine—either by heating it when necessary, rousing and expanding it, or conversely, by restraining a spirit that is too volatile. 

The nature of the spirit is primarily created and restored through things that are in harmony with those four planets <note>Jupiter, Sun, Mercury, and Venus</note>. But if you turn toward **Solar** things excessively and without discretion, you will sharpen the spirit, and eventually dry it out and dissolve it. Similarly, if you turn to **Venereal** things, you will gradually melt or blunt it. If you rely only on **Mercurial** things, you will gain very little. 

It will therefore be worthwhile to use **Jovial** things as much as possible, mixing the others in moderate amounts, and to frequently use things that are either common to all four or specific to **Jupiter**. For Jovial things are also, in a way, common to all. Generally, things belong to all of these if they have a substance that is not too fiery, nor entirely earthy, nor simply watery; their quality should be neither extremely sharp nor extremely dull, but moderate—light to the touch, somewhat soft (or at least not hard or rough), somewhat sweet to the taste, fragrant to the smell, pleasing to the sight, gentle and agreeable to the ear, and joyful to the thought. 

A certain sweetness of flavor and grace is thus common to all these planets. If the sweetness is "watery" and oily, it belongs more to **Venus**. If it is tasteless or somewhat <term>austere</term> <note>harsh or astringent</note>, it belongs to **Mercury**; these do not help the spirit much, though they are sometimes necessary to blunt its excessive sharpness. If the sweetness is clear and subtle, with a little bit of a <term>styptic</term> <note>astringent, mouth-puckering</note> and sharp flavor, it is judged properly **Jovial**. 

To this category belongs the substance of: 
* Sweet almonds, pine nuts, hazelnuts, and pistachios.
* Starch, licorice, raisins, and egg yolks.
* The meat of pullets (young chickens), pheasants, peacocks, partridges, and similar birds.
* Likewise, the roots of <term>ben</term> <note>likely Moringa or a type of sea-lavender used in Renaissance pharmacy</note> and <term>elecampane</term> <note>a medicinal root used for the lungs and digestion</note>.
* Furthermore: fragrant clear wine that is somewhat sweet and styptic, the whitest sugar, and the whitest wheat.

<term>Manna</term> <note>a sweet secretion from trees used as a mild laxative and tonic</note> also belongs to **Jupiter**, provided its virtue is strengthened by an infusion of <term>myrobalan</term> <note>a plum-like medicinal fruit</note>; otherwise, it belongs no less to **Venus** than to Jupiter. This is the substance and sweetness proper to Jupiter, which above all contributes to creating and restoring the spirit. Indeed, almost everything we mentioned in the book *On Long Life* <note>Book II of "De Vita"</note>—both for preserving youth and for the health of the elderly—is Jovial. 

If, however, the sweetness is very slight and it has much of a sharp and styptic quality, or even some bitterness, it is judged to be **Solar**. A similar logic and distinction applies to smells, for these are the brothers of flavors. The same applies to colors: "watery" colors—whites, greens, and those somewhat saffron-colored, similar to the colors of violets, roses, and lilies—and smells of that kind, refer to **Venus**, the **Moon**, and **Mercury**.

On the previous page, Ficino began categorizing which planets govern different aspects of the spirit. Here, he moves into the sensory world—colors, smells, tastes, and sounds—and how they can be used to "tune" the human spirit to specific planetary energies.</meta>

<page-num>546</page-num>
->**MARSILIO FICINO ON THE CELESTIAL LIFE**<-

The colors of sapphire, which are also called "airy," as well as fuller purples, gold mixed with silver, and perpetual greens, belong to **Jupiter**. Burning saffron-yellows, pure golds, and brighter purples belong to the **Sun**. Indeed, any colors that are vivid, or at least silken, are more "stellar" in nature. They are also potent in metals, stones, and glass because of their celestial resemblance. 

But to return to **Jupiter**: its taste and smell are like those found in a golden peach, and in similar pears or oranges, and in a lighter Malmsey wine <note>original: "uino maluatico," a sweet Mediterranean wine</note> and a light Vernaccia, as well as in green ginger, cinnamon, sweet fennel, or leopard's bane <note>original: "doronico," an herb used in Renaissance medicine</note>, if these are tasted when preserved with plenty of sugar. For these four items, along with fresh nutmeg, are primarily **Solar** if taken alone. Cloves and musk are also Solar, but by smell rather than taste or appearance. Amber is mostly Solar and **Jovial** <note>of Jupiter</note>. Saffron is Solar in all its aspects, although its color and smell are dedicated by astrologers to all the Graces <note>The three "Graces" (Jupiter, Sun, Venus) were considered the providers of life-giving benefits</note>, while its taste properly pertains to the Sun. 

Finally, all fragrant and aromatic things, insofar as they carry a pleasing odor, belong to **Jupiter**, **Venus**, and **Mercury** as much as to the **Sun**; however, among these, the sharper ones lean toward the Sun, the blunter ones toward Venus and Mercury, and those properly tempered belong to Jupiter—whether through smell, taste, hearing, sight, or touch. Furthermore, sounds and even pleasant, charming songs belong to all the Graces and Mercury. But threatening or mournful sounds represent **Mars** and **Saturn**. 

Do not wonder that we attribute so much to colors, odors, and voices. For while tastes primarily pertain to the <term>natural spirit</term> <note>the spirit responsible for nutrition and growth centered in the liver</note>, odors belong more to the <term>vital and animal spirits</term>, and colors, shapes, and voices belong to the <term>animal spirit</term> <note>the most refined spirit, centered in the brain, responsible for sensation and movement</note>. Likewise, movements of the soul—whether joyful, mournful, or steady—vehemently agitate the spirit into their own likeness: first the animal spirit, then through this the vital, and finally the natural. Indeed, because the entire spirit is somewhat fiery, entirely airy, luminous, and mobile in nature, it is similar to lights; therefore, it is suddenly moved and shaped in either direction by colors, airy voices, odors, and movements of the soul. And as the spirit itself becomes, it in turn produces a corresponding affection in the soul and a general quality in the body. Finally, when it is opportunely exposed to the Graces through those things that belong to them—since it was naturally suited to them anyway—it immediately receives the wonderful gifts of the Graces through their rays, which are both active everywhere and akin to the spirit itself.

### That natural and even artificial things possess hidden powers from the stars, through which they expose our spirit to those same stars.
### Chapter XII.

When we say that the spirit is exposed to the Graces through those things which belong to them, we mean that it is adapted not only through qualities that are seen, heard, smelled, or tasted, but also through those that are touched. Remember, therefore, that:
* **Heat** is in the first degree of **Jupiter**; in the second of the **Sun** with Jupiter; in the third of **Mars** with the Sun; in the fourth of Mars. 
* **Cold** is in the first degree of **Venus**; in the second of the **Moon**; in the third of the **Moon** with **Saturn**; in the fourth of Saturn. 
* **Moisture** is in the first degree of **Mercury** with Jupiter; in the second of **Venus** with the Moon; in the third of the **Moon** with Venus; in the fourth of the **Moon** (when it is joined to Venus and Mercury). 
* **Dryness** is in the first degree of **Jupiter**; in the second of **Mercury** with the Sun; in the third of the **Sun** with **Mars**; in the fourth of **Mars** with **Saturn**. 

In summary, from the qualities of the planets that Ptolemy writes about in the *Tetrabiblos* <note>original: "Quadripartito," Ptolemy’s foundational work on astrology</note>, we gather that the harmony forged from them all leans toward heat and moisture. For the immense heat of Mars and the Sun, combined with the tempered heat of Jupiter, overcomes the immense coldness of Saturn and the slight cold of Venus and the Moon, so that heat exceeds cold there. Likewise, the abundant moisture of the Moon and Venus (which is close to us and tempered) overcomes the great dryness of Saturn and Mars and the tempered dryness of the Sun. Since, therefore, moisture and heat dominate over cold and dryness—just as in a healthy human body tempered to celestial harmony—a certain complexion arises from the heat and dryness of the heart, the heat and moisture of the liver, and the cold and moisture of the brain, which tends toward heat and moisture, with heat reigning moderately. For the heat of the heart and liver overcomes the cold of the brain. Likewise, the moisture of the liver and brain exceeds the dryness of the heart. 

Nor would I wish us to overlook that there exists a harmony from the fixed stars common to all things, just as we have described for the planets, for astrologers believe the fixed stars are similar to them. To what purpose is all this? So that you may remember that the spirit and the body...

<page-num>547</page-num>
->**COMPARISONS. BOOK III.**<-
<sig>Mm 2</sig>

# COMPARISONS. BOOK III.

...our <note>The text begins with the end of the word "nostrum" (our), referring to the human spirit</note> spirit can be adapted to the celestial bodies through a certain tempering toward heat and moisture—whether this balance is natural or intentionally sought—and it can claim the celestial benefits for itself. However, we do not say that our spirit is prepared for these celestial gifts only through the qualities of things known to the senses <note>The "elementary" qualities: hot, cold, moist, and dry</note>, but even much more so through certain **properties** implanted in things from heaven and hidden from our senses, which are barely known even to reason. For since these properties and their effects cannot be explained by elementary power alone, it follows that they proceed uniquely from the life and spirit of the world through the rays of the stars themselves. Therefore, the spirit is affected by them most profoundly and immediately, and is powerfully exposed to celestial influences.

In this way, the **emerald**, **hyacinth**, **sapphire**, **topaz**, **ruby**, **unicorn horn**, and especially the **bezoar stone** <term>lapis bezaar: a mass found in the digestive systems of goats, prized as an antidote to poison</term> (as it is called by the Arabs) are endowed with hidden properties of grace. For this reason, if they are not only taken internally but even if they merely touch the flesh and are warmed there to release their power, they introduce a celestial force into our spirits, by which the spirits defend themselves against the plague and poisons. The proof that these and similar things perform such actions by celestial power is that even when taken in a very small weight, they have a great effect in their operation. This is almost never granted to a purely elementary quality, except perhaps for a very "celestial" fire. For a material <note>original: "Martialis," referring to the physical/elemental quality of Mars</note> power requires a great deal of matter to act effectively. A **formal** <note>In Aristotelian terms, the "form" or essence of a thing, rather than its bulk matter</note> power, however, is most potent even when the matter is minimal.

With a similar power, the **peony** of Phoebus <note>Phoebus is a name for the Sun/Apollo</note>, when touching the flesh, arms the spirits against the falling sickness <note>original: "caducum morbum," or epilepsy</note> by infusing a vapor into them. Likewise, **coral** and **chalcedony** work against the illusions of black bile <note>melancholy</note>, primarily through the power of **Jupiter** and **Venus**. Other things act through a similar property: **myrobalans** <term>myrobalani: plum-like medicinal fruits used as tonics</term> preserve youth, sharpen the minds of the elderly, and benefit the intellect and memory, chiefly because of Jupiter (who tempers the harshness of Saturn) and Mercury (who is a friend to the senses). One might even think this was the tree that existed in Paradise for the prolonging of life.

The **agate** stone is consecrated to **Mercury**; thus physicians agree it is effective for eloquence and vision, and against poisons. Serapio writes that anyone who wears a **hyacinth** <note>likely referring to a blue zircon or sapphire</note> or a seal made from it is safe from lightning; this power of the stone is widely reported, and if it possesses it, we believe it comes from Jupiter. The **eagle-stone** <term>aetites: a stone believed to contain another stone inside, like a womb</term> receives power from Lucina (that is, Venus and the Moon) so that when applied to the womb, it brings about birth quickly and very easily. Rasis, with the confirmation of Serapio, says he has experienced this frequently. Perhaps it is also from Phoebus (who pierced the Python) that **Dittany of Crete** derives its power to resist venomous creatures and pull iron from a wound.

Through the power of the **Sun**, **ginger** added to feasts wards off fainting <note>original: "syncopim"</note>. **Gentian** calms the madness of dogs and puts serpents to flight. **Vervain** is said to provide the power of prophecy, joy, purifications, and vision. **Rue** and **zedoary** act as a **Theriac** <term>theriaca: a famous ancient "universal" medicine and antidote</term> against poisons. **Frankincense** supports the vital and animal spirits against dullness, forgetfulness, and fear. **Sage** and **mint** work by the power of Jupiter: the former drives away paralysis, while the latter's scent strengthens the mind. By that same power, **cinquefoil** <note>original: "Pentaphyllon," five-leaved grass</note> resists poisons; drinking one of its leaves in wine twice a day cures a one-day fever; three leaves cure a tertian fever, and four cure a quartan fever <note>fevers associated with malaria that recur every three or four days</note>. Ancient priests used this herb in their purifications because of its purity. The **chaste tree** <note>original: "Agnus castus"</note>, by the power of Saturn, halts sexual desire, as does the **bloodstone**.

Wonderful effects usually occur where an elementary property serves a hidden property. For instance, in the **myrobalan**, it is not only that celestial power that acts to strengthen the spirit and body, but also its highly styptic <note>astringent</note> and aromatic quality, which wonderfully prevents putrefaction and dissolution. Similarly, for **saffron** to seek the heart, dilate the spirit, and provoke laughter, it is not only the hidden power of the **Sun** that works this miracle, but the very nature of saffron—subtle, expansive, aromatic, and bright—contributes to the same end.

What I say about simple ingredients, I wish to be understood also for compounds. Tell me, how does **Theriac** help us against poison? It does not draw the poison out (for it binds the bowels), nor does it change the nature of the poison entirely so quickly (for poison is not that weak). Rather, it strengthens the very thin and changeable **vital spirit** through a certain conforming proportion, to such a degree that the spirit, now strong and acting as an agent, uses the Theriac as an instrument to partly overcome the poison, partly change it, and partly drive it away from the heart. But by what proportion does Theriac achieve this without a [celestial] power? It claims a proportion that is both **Jovial** <note>of Jupiter</note> and **Phoebian** <note>of the Sun</note>, which it seems to have acquired from the mixing of many things according to a certain ratio. Indeed, there is a triple power in it: first, this celestial power I just mentioned; and second, a celestial... <note>The text cuts off; the catchword is "stis," likely part of "coelestis"</note>

<summary>Ficino explains that certain stones and herbs possess "occult properties" derived from the stars, which allow them to strengthen the human spirit and act as antidotes to poison or disease. He argues that these substances work through celestial "form" rather than physical bulk, emphasizing the healing powers of Jupiter and the Sun.</summary>
<keywords>occult properties, spiritus, planetary medicine, Theriac, gems, herbalism, Marsilio Ficino, Jupiter, Sun, pharmacology</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on how celestial influences are captured in physical substances, moving from specific stones to the complex composition of "theriac"—a famed ancient medicine—and the importance of astrological timing (election) for making these remedies effective.</meta>

<page-num>548</page-num>
<header>MARSILIO FICINO ON THE CELESTIAL LIFE</header>

...celestial <note>The text begins mid-sentence: "coelestis"</note> property found first in herbs and aromatics, from which, once selected, the medicine is properly composed, and which serves the previously mentioned power toward the same end. Furthermore, there is another power in many of its parts, more elementary than celestial, yet of such a kind that it helps to fortify the spirit—I mean its styptic <note>astringent or contracting</note> and aromatic qualities. The former strengthens the spirit, while the latter nourishes it. Therefore, **theriac** <term>theriaca: a complex "universal" antidote and medicine made of dozens of ingredients, including snake flesh</term> has gained a wonderful power against approaching old age and poison, because three powers within it conspire toward that same goal: one is celestial, acquired through the skillful mixing of ingredients; another is also celestial, but naturally inherent in its individual parts; and the third is purely elementary. 

But that first power I mentioned—acquired from heaven—would be far more admirable if not only the proportions of **Jupiter** and the **Sun** were used in its creation from such things, but if a favorable time were also chosen for this task by observing the heavenly bodies. For just as a body relates to its place and time, so does movement and action relate to time. Therefore, just as certain bodies and their forms coalesce and are preserved in specific places and times, so too do certain specific actions gain their efficacy from specific times. Socrates indicates this in the *Alcibiades*, and Proclus explains it. Surely observing this, **Pythagoras** named "the good" and the "perfection of things" as **Opportunity** <note>original: "opportunitatem," translating the Greek *kairos*, the "right moment"</note>. 

For according to Pythagoras and Plato, the first principle is the measure of all things in such a way that it distributed different places and times to different bodies and actions. Just as certain things are not born successfully or preserved anywhere else but *here*, nor at any other time but *then*, so a material action, a fear, or a particular outcome does not obtain its efficacy and perfect effect at any other time than when the harmony of the heavens resonates with it from all sides. This harmony is thought to have such great power that it grants a frequently miraculous virtue not only to the labors of farmers and the skills of doctors (blended through herbs and aromatics), but even to **images** <note>astrological talismans</note> which are made by astrologers from metals and stones. But the subject of images now requires its own chapter. 

As for choosing the right hours for actions and works, this is strongly confirmed by **Ptolemy** <note>The famous 2nd-century astronomer and geographer</note> where he says in the *Centiloquium* <note>a collection of 100 astrological aphorisms</note>: "He who chooses what is better seems to differ in no way from one who has this by nature." By these words, he seems to confirm both the power of the heavens and the power of our own judgment and choice. **Albertus Magnus** <note>A 13th-century Dominican friar and influential philosopher</note> also says in the *Mirror*: "The freedom of choice is not constrained by choosing a praiseworthy hour; rather, to despise the choice of an hour in the beginnings of great works is a recklessness of judgment, not freedom."

---

->On the power of images according to the ancients, and medicines acquired<-
->from heaven. Chapter XIV.<-

# P
tolemy says in the *Centiloquium* that the forms of lower things are subject to the "faces" of the heavens, and that the wise men of old were accustomed to fabricate certain **images** at the time when similar faces entered the sky, acting as the models for the lower things. **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer</note> confirms this there, saying: "An effective image of a serpent can be made when the Moon enters the celestial Serpent <note>likely the constellation Hydra or Draco</note>, or gazes upon it favorably." Similarly, an image of a **Scorpion** is effective when the Moon enters the sign of Scorpio and this sign holds one of the four angles <note>the most powerful points in an astrological chart: the ascendant, descendant, midheaven, or lower midheaven</note>. 

He says this was done in Egypt in his own time, and that he was present when a figure was imprinted on incense from a seal of a Scorpion made on a **bezoar stone** <note>original: "lapide Bezahar"</note>; this was given in a drink to a man whom a scorpion had stung, and he was cured immediately. **Hahameth** the physician affirms that this is effectively done, with **Serapion** <note>a 9th-century medical writer</note> confirming it. Furthermore, Haly relates that a wise man known to him there made images by similar industry that could move—just as we read of one made, I know not how, by **Archytas** <note>A Greek philosopher said to have built a mechanical wooden pigeon</note>. 

**Hermes Trismegistus** <note>the legendary "Thrice-Great" founder of Hermeticism</note> also says the Egyptians used to make such things from certain materials of the world, and were accustomed to timely insert into them the souls of **demons** <note>in the Neoplatonic sense: mediating spirits, not necessarily "evil"</note>, as well as the soul of his grandfather **Mercury**. Likewise, he says that the souls of a certain **Phoebus**, and of **Isis** and **Osiris**, descended into statues in this way, to either benefit or even harm humans. Similar to this is the story that **Prometheus** stole life and celestial light by means of a certain clay figure. Furthermore, the **Magi** who followed **Zoroaster**, in order to summon a spirit from **Hecate**, used a certain golden ball marked with celestial characters, in which a sapphire was inserted; it was spun by a thong made of bull's hide, while they chanted incantations.

He cites ancient authorities like Ptolemy, Hermes Trismegistus, and Albertus Magnus to justify the use of astrological timing in both medicine and the animation of sacred objects.</summary>

<page-num>549</page-num>

->ON OBTAINING LIFE FROM THE HEAVENS. BOOK III.<-

But I willingly omit incantations. For **Psellus the Platonist** <note>Michael Psellus, an 11th-century Byzantine philosopher and historian.</note> also disapproves of and mocks them. The **Hebrews** too, raised in Egypt, learned to build the golden calf—as their own **Astrologers** believe—to catch the favor of **Venus** and the **Moon** against the influence of **Scorpio** and **Mars**, which was hostile to the Jews. **Porphyry** <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher (c. 234–305 AD) who wrote a famous letter to the Egyptian priest Anebo.</note> also, in his letter to Anebo, testifies that images are effective, and that at certain specific times, when they exhaled their own proper vapors, aerial spirits <note>original: "dæmonas," referring to mediating spirits, not necessarily "demons" in the modern evil sense</note> were immediately accustomed to enter them. **Iamblichus** confirms that in materials which are naturally in harmony with the higher powers, and which have been opportunely and rightly collected from everywhere and fused together, not only celestial but even spiritual and divine powers and effects can be received. **Proclus** and **Synesius** say entirely the same thing.

Indeed, works for health which can be made by physicians skilled in Astrology through substances composed of many things—that is, powders, liquids, ointments, and **electuaries** <term>electuaria: medicinal pastes made by mixing powders with honey or syrup</term>—seem to have a more probable and better-known reasoning within them than images do. This is partly because powders, liquids, ointments, and electuaries, when opportunely prepared, receive celestial influences more easily and quickly than the harder materials from which images are usually made; and partly because they are either taken internally when they have already been celestially affected and are transformed into us, or at least when applied externally they cling more closely and finally penetrate. It is also because images are constructed from only one or very few things, whereas medical works can consist of as many as one chooses. 

For instance, if a hundred gifts of the **Sun** or **Jupiter** were scattered through a hundred plants, animals, and similar things, you could compose these hundred things found by you at the same time and make them into one form, in which you would now seem to have almost the whole Sun and Jupiter. You know, surely, that a lower nature cannot capture all the powers of a higher nature in one single thing; therefore, those powers are dispersed among many natures here with us, and can be more conveniently gathered through the works of physicians and similar means than through images. 

Furthermore, images made of wood perhaps have little power; for wood is perhaps too hard to easily receive celestial influence, and less tenacious in retaining it if it has received it. And generally, after it has been torn from the bowels of mother earth, it soon loses almost all the vigor of its worldly life and is easily changed into another quality. But small stones and metals, even if they seem harder for receiving a celestial gift, nevertheless retain it longer, as **Iamblichus** confirms, if they have received it. By their very hardness, they contain the traces and gifts of worldly life for a very long time after being uprooted, which they once possessed while clinging to the earth. Therefore, for this reason at least, they are judged to be suitable materials for receiving and holding celestial things. 

It is also probable, as I said in the previous book, that such beautiful things cannot be forged under the earth except by some great effort of the heavens, and that the virtue once impressed by that effort lasts within them. For the heavens labored for a very long time in cooking and compressing these things. But since you cannot easily compose many such things together, you are forced to diligently seek out which metal among others is foremost in the order of some star, or which stone is highest in that order, so that at least in one supreme thing of a whole genus and order, you may grasp the rest according to your strength, and borrow celestial things agreeable to this through such a vessel. 

For example, if in the **Solar** order under a **Phoebean** <note>original: "Phœbeo," meaning relating to Phoebus Apollo, or the Sun</note> man, the Goshawk or the Cock holds the highest place among animals, the balsam or the laurel among plants, gold among metals, the carbuncle or **pantaura** <note>A legendary magnetic stone said to be solar in nature.</note> among stones, and glowing air among elements (for fire itself is judged to belong to **Mars**). When we say, however, that the influence of the Sun, Jupiter, or Venus should be increased, we understand this by general reasoning; yet not for someone in whose **nativity** <note>birth chart</note> one of these appears as the **slayer** <term>interfector: the "killing planet" or anaretic point in a horoscope, believed to signify the end of life</term>.

### On the orders of things hanging from the stars, such as the Solar ones and similar, and how a spirit becomes Solar. Chapter 14.

I have said elsewhere that from above, from each and every star (to speak in the **Platonic** way), a series of things proper to it hangs all the way down to the lowest things. Under the heart of **Scorpio** <note>The star Antares.</note> itself, after spirits and men of that kind, we can place the animal the scorpion, and also the herb **Asterion** <note>original: "stellar," likely a species of Aster or a phosphorescent plant.</note>—that is, the "starry" herb—similar in shape to a star and shining at night, which physicians report has the quality of a rose and possesses a wonderful power against diseases of the genitals. Under the celestial **Serpent** or the **Serpent-bearer** <note>The constellations Serpens and Ophiuchus.</note>, they place **Saturn**, and in a certain way **Jupiter**. After these, the spirits who often take the forms of serpents. Furthermore, similar...

## MARSILIO FICINO ON OBTAINING LIFE FROM THE HEAVENS

...men, living serpents, the herb serpentaria, and the stone Draconite <note>original: "Draconitem"; a legendary gemstone supposedly found in the heads of dragons</note> which is born in the head of a dragon. Likewise, those things known by the common name "Serpentine." And besides these, I shall bring forth more in what follows. Under the Solar star—that is, Sirius <note>Ficino identifies Sirius, the Dog Star, as having a primary Solar nature</note>—one finds the Sun first, then the Phoebean spirits <note>original: "demonas... Phoebeos"; spirits associated with Apollo/the Sun</note>, whom **Proclus** <note>A 5th-century Neoclassical philosopher who wrote extensively on "sympathy" between the heavens and earth</note> testifies have sometimes appeared to men in the form of lions or roosters. Next are men and beasts who are very similar to the Sun. Then come Phoebean plants, metals, and likewise little stones, as well as steam and glowing air. By a similar reasoning, they believe that from any star in the firmament, a fabric of things descends step-by-step through a specific Planet under that star's particular property. 

If, therefore (as I was saying), you appropriately gather all Solar things through any step of that order—namely such men, or something from such a man, likewise animals, plants, metals, stones, and whatever pertains to these—you drink in the power of the Sun everywhere, and in a certain way, the natural faculty of the Solar spirits. You should consider the same said for the other planets. Indeed, Solar men are such as I have described before: those born when **Leo** is ascending and the **Sun** is either occupying or beholding it, and those born under **Aries** in a similar way. Solar, too, is the blood drawn from the left arm of such well-disposed people. Phoebean animals include the crocodile, the hawk, the lion, the rooster, the swan, and the crow. Nor is there any other reason why the lion fears the rooster, except that in the Phoebean order, the rooster is superior to the lion. For the same reason, says **Proclus**, an Apolline spirit <note>original: "Apollineum dæmonem"</note>, which had sometimes appeared in the form of a lion, immediately vanished when a rooster was presented. 

Truly, the heart is the most Solar part in these animals. I also believe that the seal <note>original: "marinun uitulum"; literally "sea-calf"</note> is subject to the heart of the celestial **Leo**; for this very reason, its hide—when cinched by a bare buckle made from its own bone—is said to relieve pain in the kidneys. For Astrologers are accustomed to use the influences of that constellation against such pains. By perhaps the same reasoning, this skin is said to protect us from lightning. Among plants, the palm is Phoebean, and especially the laurel, which by its power repels poisons and lightning. The ash tree, with a similar faculty, keeps poisonous things at a great distance. That the lotus is Phoebean is testified by its round fruits and the unfolding of its leaves by day and their closing by night. That the peony is Phoebean is indicated not only by its power, but by its name <note>The name "Paeonia" is derived from Paean, an epithet of Apollo as the healer</note>. To the same category belong flowers and herbs that contract as the Sun departs and immediately unfold as it returns, continually turning toward the Sun. Furthermore, there is gold and the *Elitis* stone <note>A "sunstone" or variety of feldspar that reflects light</note>, which imitates the Sun with golden rays. Likewise, the stone called the "Sun's Eye," having the shape of a pupil from which light flashes. Again, the carbuncle which glows at night, or the *Pantataura* <note>A legendary "all-bull" stone mentioned in ancient lapidaries</note> which contains within itself all the powers of stones, just as gold contains those of metals and the Sun those of the stars. 

Finally, many things have been signified to us in the higher realms; from which (if it be permitted) you may prepare under the dominion of the Sun an **electuary** <term>electuarium: a medicinal paste made of powders and honey</term> or an ointment. You may make it from that blood, the hearts of those animals, the leaves and fruits of the aforementioned trees, as well as the flowers, herbs, and gold leaf. You might even add the powders of the "pupils" <note>likely referring to the "eye" stones mentioned above</note>, along with saffron, balsam, aromatic reed, frankincense, musk, amber, aloe wood, ginger, mastic, spikenard, cinnamon, citron bark <note>original: "dronico citri cortice"</note>, zedoary, nutmeg, mace, and cloves. Mix these with yellow or golden honey—balsamic, mastic, laurel, or nard-flavored—to soothe the heart, stomach, and head, either internally or externally, so that the **spirit** <note>In Ficino's philosophy, "spirit" is the thin, vaporous substance that connects the physical body to the soul</note> may then become Solar. From all these things, I say, or at least from many of them, something should be composed while the Sun is dominant. You should also begin to use it under that same dominance, provided that you also dress in Solar clothes, live in Solar places, and see, hear, smell, imagine, think of, and desire Solar things. Likewise, you should imitate both the dignity of life and the gifts of the Sun. Dwell among Solar men and plants, and touch the laurel frequently. 

However, it will be safer for your health to mix Jovial <note>from Jupiter</note> and Venereal <note>from Venus</note> things with the Solar ones. Venusian moisture especially acts as a moderator for Solar heat, such as the water and juice of roses and violets. But I have partly composed such medicines first in my book *On Caring for the Health of Scholars*, then in the book *On Long Life*; partly I have described those composed by others, and partly I have tempered them. Likewise, what herbs have wondrous powers against epidemic and poison from the Sun and **Jupiter**, we have discussed in the book *Against the Plague*. Among these is *Perforata* <note>St. John’s Wort</note>, which is called "demon-flee" <note>original: "fugadæmon"</note>; it is thought to keep the harmful vapors of evil spirits away from us by no other faculty than that of celestial graces—just as among herbs and stones, coral seems to do the same. Indeed, the Lunar herb handed down by **Mercury**, with its blue and round leaves, producing one leaf daily as the Moon waxes and shedding one as it wanes, promises "Lunar years" to the one who uses it.

THINGS TO BE COMPARED. BOOK III.

## On the power of images according to the ancients and of medicines. And how medicines are far more powerful than images.
### Chapter XV.

**I**f you happen upon those little stones of Phoebus <note>Solar stones, named after Phoebus Apollo, the sun god</note> which we described just a moment ago, there will be no need to engrave images upon them. You should simply hang them from your neck, set in gold with saffron-colored silk threads, at a time when the Sun is traveling through Aries or Leo and is either rising or occupying the middle of the sky <term>mid-heaven</term>, and is in aspect to the Moon. However, **Proclus** <note>A Neoplatonic philosopher who wrote on the "sympathies" between heaven and earth</note> relates that the stones in the series of the Moon are much more powerful. First among these is *Selenite* <note>Moonstone; from the Greek 'Selene' for Moon</note>, which not only imitates the Moon in its shape, but also in its motion, moving along with the Moon. If you should happen to find this, and hang it from your neck set in silver with a silver thread when the Moon is entering Cancer or Taurus and holding the angles favorable to her, it will return to you a spirit that is, ultimately, lunar. This happens because the stone itself, warmed by you, continuously inserts its lunar virtue into your spirits. He lists another little stone called *helioselinon* <note>original: "helioselinon"; a stone traditionally thought to combine the properties of the Sun (Helios) and Moon (Selene)</note>, which naturally possesses the image of the Sun joined to the Moon. Therefore, if anyone places this—enclosed in silver with gilded threads—around their neck when the Moon is in her own home <note>the zodiac sign of Cancer</note> or in the home of the Sun <note>the zodiac sign of Leo</note>, or meets with the Sun in the same minute, and holds her proper angles, he will carry away a solar as well as a lunar spirit—or at least such a spirit as the Moon becomes when joined to the Sun through its center. Here you see the scattered gifts of Phoebus, like the limbs of Osiris, being gathered together by his sister Phoebe <note>the Moon</note> as if she were Isis <note>Ficino uses the Egyptian myth of Isis gathering the pieces of her husband Osiris to explain how the Moon collects and focuses the Sun's light</note>. 

But I wish we could easily find a solar or lunar stone somewhere that was as powerful in their order as we have the magnet <term>lodestone</term> and iron under the series of the Northern Pole. Indeed, they say that **Apollonius of Tyana** <note>A famous first-century miracle-worker and philosopher</note> found a solar stone among the Indians, specifically a stone named *Pantaurus* <note>A legendary gem said to attract other stones</note>, which glitters like fire and is born four paces under the earth. It is said to have so much spirit in it that it swells, and the earth is often split where such a stone is conceived; it draws other stones to itself just as a magnet draws iron. But this *Herculean stone* <note>The magnet or lodestone</note> seizes us even more powerfully for our contemplation at present. We see in the sailors' compass the needle, balanced and touched at its tip by the Magnet, move toward the Bear <note>The constellation Ursa Major, the Great Bear, indicating the North Star</note>. It is drawn there because the Magnet is moved by the virtue of the Bear which prevails in this stone, and from here it is transferred into the iron, and it draws both toward the Bear. Such a virtue was infused from the beginning and is continuously nourished by the stars' rays. Perhaps amber <note>original: "Succinum"</note> behaves this way toward the other pole and toward straws. 

But tell me, meanwhile, why does the Magnet everywhere draw iron? It is not because they are similar, otherwise a Magnet would draw a Magnet, and much more so would iron draw iron. It is not because it is higher in the order of bodies—on the contrary, a metal is higher than a little stone. What then? Both are enclosed in the order following the Bear, but the Magnet holds a higher rank in that specific property of the Bear, while iron holds a lower one. In the same context of things, the higher draws that which is lower, and turns it toward itself, or agitates it in whatever other way, or affects it with a virtue previously infused. The lower, in turn, is turned toward the higher by the same arrangement, or is otherwise agitated or entirely affected. Thus, in the series of the Sun, a lower man admires a higher one; in the Jovian <note>related to Jupiter</note> order he venerates him; in the Martian order he fears him; in the Venusian order the lower is seized by the heat of love for the higher and deserts himself; in the Mercurial order the lower always learns from the higher or is persuaded by him; in the Lunar order the lower often takes his motion from the higher; and in the Saturnian order, his rest. 

I, however, having explored these things this far, was greatly pleased; and while I was still a young man, I thought to engrave the figure of the celestial Bear upon a Magnet as best I could when the Moon looked favorably upon it, and then to hang it from my neck by an iron wire. I hoped, indeed, that I would thus finally become a master of the virtue of that star. But after I had explored it longer, I found at last that the influences of that star are mostly Saturnine and Martian <note>influenced by Saturn and Mars, traditionally the "malefic" or difficult planets</note>. I learned from the Platonists that evil demons are mostly Northern, which even the Hebrew astronomers confess, placing harmful and Martian demons in the North, but propitious and Jovian <note>associated with Jupiter</note> ones in the South. I learned from the theologians and from **Iamblichus** <note>A Neoplatonic philosopher who wrote on magic and theurgy</note> that the makers of images are often occupied and deceived by evil demons. Indeed, I saw a little stone brought to Florence from India, taken there from the head of a dragon <note>A "Draconite" stone</note>; it was round, in the shape of a coin, naturally marked with many points in order, like stars. When it was soaked in vinegar, it moved a little in a straight line, or rather obliquely, and soon was carried in a circle until the vapor of the vinegar exhaled. I certainly thought that a stone of this kind possessed the nature of the celestial Dragon...

and as if a figure, it also receives its motion, insofar as through the spirit of vinegar or a stronger wine, it is made more familiar to that Dragon <note>The constellation Draco</note> or the firmament. He who wears this and frequently bathes it in vinegar might perhaps receive some power from that Dragon, which with its twin coils entwines the Great Bear on one side and the Little Bear on the other. There also exists near Scorpio the Serpent-bearer <note>Serpentarius, now known as Ophiuchus</note>, looking like a man girded by a serpent, holding the serpent's head in his right hand and the tail in his left, with his knees as if bent and his head tilted slightly back. Indeed, I have read that the Magi advised the King of the Persians to engrave this image on a stone of Hematite <note>A reddish-black iron ore stone; the name comes from the Greek word for blood</note>, which he should enclose in a gold ring, provided that he inserts the root of the "serpent-plant" <term>serpentaria</term> <note>likely *Aristolochia* or *Dracunculus*, plants believed to cure snakebites</note> between the stone and the gold. For they say the wearer of this ring will be safe from poison and poisonous diseases—specifically if you make it while the Moon is looking upon the Serpent-bearer. **Pietro d'Abano** <note>original: "Petrus Aponensis"; a famous 13th-century physician and astrologer</note> confirmed this image. 

But I, for my part, if that ring has such power, think it claims it for itself from the heavens not so much through the figure, as through materials of this kind, composed in such a manner and at such a time. Remember that little stones born within animals—provided the animal does not grow weak therefrom, as in the dragon, the rooster, the swallow, and others—are almost as effective as stones born in the earth, and are referred to the same stars to which these animals belong. Hence the *Alectorius* <note>The "cock-stone," a crystal-like stone supposedly found in the gizzards of old roosters</note>, drawn from the stomach of an old rooster, is potent with Solar power; **Dioscorides** <note>A Greek physician and botanist of the 1st century AD</note> says it has often been found that he who carries this stone in his mouth remains undefeated in battle. He also says that the *Chelidonium* <note>The "swallow-stone," from the Greek 'chelidon' for swallow</note>, dug out of a swallow, if it is reddish, cures the melancholic and makes one lovable and fit. This it truly holds from Jupiter, through those principles we have stated: namely, that everywhere below the Moon there exist "stellar" things. 

That truly Platonic saying is strongly confirmed: that this machine of the world is so connected with itself that celestial things are on earth in a terrestrial condition, and in turn, terrestrial things are in heaven with celestial dignity; and in the hidden life of the world and the Mind that is the queen of the world, celestial things are present, yet with a vital and intellectual property and excellence at once. Furthermore, through these things, some even confirm that magical principle: namely, that because lower things are in harmony with higher things, celestial things can, at opportune times, be drawn in a certain way to men; and even through celestial things, those things "above the heavens" <note>referring to divine or angelic powers beyond the physical stars</note> may be reconciled to us, or perhaps even instilled in us—though let those authors see to this last point. 

Truly, it seems probable enough (as we have said) that such a thing can be done by a certain art that rightly and opportunely gathers many things into one—both for the reasons we assigned above, and because when many things of this kind are gathered by a physician and astrologer, and are crushed, mixed, and "cooked" <note>processed or refined</note> under a certain star, they gradually undergo a new form through the process of concoction and fermentation. They acquire this form through a certain celestial nourishment, with the rays then acting from within, and therefore the form is celestial. 

However, when a metal or a stone is carved in a single moment, it does not seem to receive a new quality, but only a "figure" <note>a shape</note>. Nor does that motion proceed through the proper steps of digestion which natural alteration and generation are accustomed to observe. Since celestial nature, as the ruler of lower nature, usually proceeds by a certain natural tenor and breathes upon those things that proceed in such a way, most people rightly distrust that images of this kind have any celestial power. I too am often in doubt; and unless all of antiquity and all the Astrologers thought they had wonderful power, I would deny they had any. Indeed, I would not deny it entirely, for I think (unless someone persuades me otherwise) they have at least some power for good health, especially when the material is chosen with reason—though I think far greater power resides in medicines and ointments blended with stellar favor. 

But what I meant just now when I said "the material chosen with reason," I shall declare in what follows. Those things which can be alleged for images from the opinion of the Magi or Astrologers to interpret **Plotinus**, I shall bring forward briefly hereafter—provided I first warn you here not to think that I approve of the use of images, but that I am narrating it. For I use medicines tempered to the sky, not images, and thus I advise others daily. But you, if you concede that God has inserted wonderful virtues into things below the Moon, then concede even more wonderful ones to celestial things. Furthermore, if you judge it lawful for a man to use lower things for his good health, judge that it is also lawful to use higher things, and to temper lower things to the pattern of the higher through the artifice of physicians, just as they were also tempered by God from the beginning.
